sources.title: Regional utilization survey
sources.excerpt: Across a 24-system sample, telehealth utilization remains materially above pre-2020 levels for behavioral health, medication follow-up, and chronic-care check-ins. Rural and mobility-limited patients continue to rely on virtual follow-up capacity.

sources.title: Revised payer brief on selected parity extensions
sources.excerpt: Several large commercial plans and state Medicaid programs extended payment parity for selected behavioral-health and some chronic-care telehealth follow-up services through multiyear updates. Parity is stable enough to justify selective expansion with payer-by-payer validation, but it is not universal outside the targeted lines.

sources.title: Revised state-cluster compliance assessment
sources.excerpt: Two high-volume state clusters now have materially tighter licensing, consent, and audit requirements. Expansion should use state-clustered rollout sequencing and stronger local compliance support rather than a uniform multistate rollout.

sources.title: Segmented access and continuity analysis
sources.excerpt: Access benefits are strongest for behavioral-health follow-up and for rural or mobility-limited patient segments. Evidence is weaker for broad chronic-care expansion outside those targeted populations.

sources.title: Sharpened chronic-care cost and utilization caution memo
sources.excerpt: Broad savings claims are not supported. Chronic-care follow-up expansion is especially vulnerable to low-acuity utilization growth unless triage, interval controls, and substitution rules are enforced.

sources.title: Clinical workflow fit note
sources.excerpt: Telehealth performs best for medication management, therapy, routine chronic-care follow-up, and monitoring. It is less appropriate for new diagnostic workups, imaging-dependent care, and complaints requiring physical examination.

sources.title: Broadband access brief
sources.excerpt: Connectivity gaps and digital literacy barriers remain concentrated in some rural and elderly populations, creating adoption limits even where demand for virtual care is strong.
